privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicy.metaDescription: How TradeCatch collects, uses, and protects information submitted through this website and the systems we manage.

sections.heading: Who this policy covers
sections.body: This policy applies to TradeCatch, operated by Ara Ghahramanyan from the Greater Montreal area, Quebec, Canada, with respect to personal information collected through this website and the systems we manage on behalf of contractor clients. It is written to reflect Quebec's private-sector privacy legislation (the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, as amended by Law 25) and applicable federal privacy law (PIPEDA).

sections.heading: Information we collect
sections.body: We collect information you provide directly when you request a demo: name, company, trade, email, phone number, city, and qualification answers. Once you are a customer, we also process, within the agreed scope, names, phone numbers, addresses, service-request details and photos; call and text content and metadata; the contact details of the people who receive your alerts; appointments and calendar availability when scheduling is switched on; and activity in your account. We also collect technical data and, with your consent, analytics data as explained in our Cookie Policy.

sections.heading: Purposes and legal basis for collection
sections.body: We use this information to respond to demo requests, schedule calls and prepare proposals and, once you are a customer, to answer calls, collect and route requests, run text follow-ups, manage appointments and show everything in your account. The applicable basis depends on context, including consent, pre-contractual steps, the service agreement, and legal obligations. We do not sell personal information.

sections.heading: SMS and email communication consent
sections.body: Contacting you about your specific demo request (by phone, email, or text) is a necessary service communication, not optional marketing. It is covered by the required consent checkbox on our forms. Marketing emails (tips, offers, updates) are separate, optional, opt-in, and never pre-checked, consistent with Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation (CASL). Message and data rates may apply to SMS. We record the exact wording, source form, and timestamp of each consent given, and honour opt-out or unsubscribe requests without delay.

sections.heading: Data sharing and service providers
sections.body: We share information with service providers that support our operations under agreements requiring them to protect your data and use it only for the purpose we specify. As of this writing that includes: Resend (transactional email delivery), Google Analytics 4 (site analytics, only after cookie consent), Cloudflare (website hosting and delivery, including Turnstile bot-abuse prevention on our forms), and Twilio (SMS/voice for missed-call recovery when enabled). We do not share your information for third-party advertising.

sections.heading: Cross-border data transfers
sections.body: Some service providers may process or store personal information outside Quebec or Canada, including in the United States. Before a provider processes personal information outside Quebec, we assess the privacy factors required by law and determine the appropriate contractual or other safeguards. Processing locations and applicable measures are described in client documentation or agreements when required.

sections.heading: Data retention schedule
sections.body: We target retention of up to 24 months after the last interaction for demo requests and call and text records, unless the law, an earlier deletion request, or a client agreement requires otherwise. Automated purging for those categories depends on durable storage and the scheduled task; until deployment is verified, it is performed manually. Other customer data, such as website leads, quotes, appointments and related logs, follows the retention term in the client agreement and is deleted manually until full lifecycle automation is in place. Analytics data follows Google Analytics’ retention settings.

sections.heading: Your privacy rights
sections.body: Under Quebec and Canadian privacy law you may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal information, and may withdraw consent to non-essential processing at any time, by contacting our privacy contact below. We will respond within the timelines required by law.

sections.heading: How to reach us or file a complaint
sections.body: For any privacy question or request, contact our privacy contact at contact@tradecatch.ca. If you believe we have not resolved your concern, you may file a complaint with the Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec (CAI).

sections.heading: Security and incident reporting
sections.body: We apply technical and organizational safeguards (encryption in transit, access restrictions, security headers, and the controls described in our security practices) appropriate to the sensitivity of the information involved. In the event of a confidentiality incident presenting a risk of serious harm, we will notify affected individuals and the CAI as required by Law 25.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
sections.body: We may update this policy as our practices or legal obligations change. Material changes will be reflected in the "last updated" date above.

termsOfService.metaDescription: The terms governing the use of the TradeCatch website and the revenue recovery systems we design, install, and manage.

sections.heading: Services
sections.body: TradeCatch designs, installs, and manages automated communication workflows for contractor businesses. Two plans are offered. Essential answers calls in French and English, captures customer requests, and follows up by text. Professional includes everything in Essential and adds appointment scheduling, including Google Calendar, which is switched on for your business once it has been tested with you. Both plans are set up for your business during onboarding. Call and text usage is subject to the monthly allowance of your plan, and usage past it is not charged without your confirmation. Call transfer, voice cloning, bulk messaging and CRM integrations are not offered. The optional website service is a separate one-time project. Nothing in these terms is a guarantee of results or of uninterrupted service.

sections.heading: Client responsibilities
sections.body: Clients are responsible for providing accurate business information, approving message content and urgent-call rules before launch, and ensuring that licensed staff handle diagnosis, pricing, and safety-related decisions.

sections.heading: Service limitations
sections.body: The system does not diagnose technical, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, medical, or safety conditions, and does not guarantee any specific volume of leads, bookings, or revenue. Results depend on factors outside our control, including demand, pricing, and service quality.

sections.heading: Emergency handling
sections.body: The system flags urgent calls using rules the client approves in advance and tells callers to contact emergency services when anyone may be in danger. It does not transfer calls and does not itself assess or respond to emergencies. Handling of urgent or safety-related situations remains the responsibility of the contractor and their qualified personnel at all times, and clients must maintain their own emergency-response process independent of this system.

sections.heading: Fees and payment
sections.body: The one-time setup fee is paid at checkout. The monthly fee for your plan is charged from one month after setup and every month after that. The optional website service is a separate one-time fee, charged only if you select it. All prices are in Canadian dollars and are shown on the pricing page. Late payment may result in suspension of services.

sections.heading: Cancellation and refunds
sections.body: Either party may terminate the management agreement with written notice according to the term specified in your proposal. Setup fees are non-refundable once work has begun; unused prepaid management fees for the remainder of a notice period are not refunded except as required by applicable Quebec consumer-protection law.

sections.heading: Electronic acceptance
sections.body: Proposals, this agreement, and related documents may be accepted electronically (including by e-signature or by written confirmation such as email). Electronic acceptance has the same legal effect as a handwritten signature, consistent with Quebec's legal framework for information technology (An Act to establish a legal framework for information technology).

sections.heading: Limitation of liability

cookiePolicy.title: Cookie Policy
cookiePolicy.metaDescription: Which cookies this website uses, why, and how to manage your preferences.

sections.heading: What are cookies
sections.body: Cookies are small text files stored on your device that help websites function and let us understand how visitors use the site. This site also uses similar browser storage (localStorage) to remember your cookie choice itself.

sections.heading: Cookies and storage we use
sections.body: Essential: a language-preference cookie (NEXT_LOCALE) remembers whether you're browsing in French or English; none of our own session cookies are otherwise strictly required for core browsing, and your cookie-consent choice is saved in your browser's localStorage so we don't ask again every visit. Analytics: Google Analytics 4 sets cookies (such as _ga) to measure traffic and usage, and only loads after you accept analytics cookies below. Security: Cloudflare Turnstile may set short-lived, essential cookies while verifying that a form submission is not automated; these are not used for tracking. We do not use cookies for third-party advertising.

sections.heading: Managing your cookie choice
sections.body: You can accept all cookies, reject non-essential cookies, or open detailed preferences using the banner shown on your first visit. All three options are equally easy to choose. You can change your choice at any time using the "Manage cookies" link in the footer, or by changing your browser settings to block or delete cookies.

accessibilityStatement.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibilityStatement.metaDescription: Our accessibility target for this website, known limitations, and how to report an accessibility issue.

sections.heading: Our commitment
sections.body: We aim to provide a website that is accessible to the widest possible audience and are working toward conformance with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at Level AA. WCAG is a technical standard, not a legal designation. We treat conformance with it as our working benchmark rather than a claim of legal compliance in any particular jurisdiction.

sections.heading: Accessibility features implemented
sections.body: Semantic landmarks and heading structure on every page; a skip-to-main-content link; full keyboard operability for the navigation, mobile menu, forms, and the demo-booking wizard, including a focus trap and Escape-to-close in the mobile menu and returning focus to the trigger on close; visible focus indicators on all interactive elements; support for the prefers-reduced-motion setting; form fields with programmatic labels, required-state and error messaging that is announced to assistive technology and linked to the relevant field; and alt text on informative images with decorative graphics hidden from assistive technology.

sections.heading: Known limitations
sections.body: This site is under active development. Some third-party embeds, such as the Cloudflare Turnstile widget, are provided by external vendors and may not fully match our own accessibility standard. Automated and manual testing cannot catch every barrier. We review and address issues as they are identified rather than treating any point-in-time audit as a guarantee of full conformance.

sections.heading: Standards and legal compliance
sections.body: TradeCatch is based in Québec and primarily serves contractors in Québec; we may also serve clients elsewhere in Canada and in the United States. Accessibility legal obligations vary by jurisdiction (for example, Québec’s rules under the Act to secure handicapped persons in the exercise of their rights, and, where applicable to U.S. visitors, the Americans with Disabilities Act) and can differ from the WCAG technical standard described above. We do not claim certified legal compliance with any specific accessibility law, and we recommend anyone with a specific legal question consult qualified counsel in the relevant jurisdiction.

sections.heading: Feedback, alternate formats, and contact
sections.body: If you encounter an accessibility barrier on this site, or need information from this site in another format, please contact us at contact@tradecatch.ca describing the page and the issue (or the format you need). We will work to address genuine barriers and respond to format requests in a reasonable timeframe.

platform.transcript: You're busy on the job. Your phone rings, but you can't answer. And just like that, a customer can move on to your competitor. Meet the TradeCatch Receptionist. It answers your calls as your business, in French or English, even when you can't pick up. Receptionist: Thank you for calling NorthStar Plumbing! How can I help you today? Caller: Hi, my kitchen sink is leaking. Do you do repairs in Laval? Receptionist: Yes, we serve Laval and the surrounding area. Is the leak causing any flooding? Caller: No, but I'd like someone to come by tomorrow. Receptionist: Of course. What time works best for you? Caller: Around ten in the morning. Receptionist: Perfect. I've sent your request for tomorrow at 10 a.m. to the team. They'll text you shortly to confirm. Caller: My basement is flooding! I need to speak to someone right now. Receptionist: I understand, this is urgent. I'm connecting you to the on-call technician right away. Emergencies you define go straight to your on-call line. Every call lands in one workspace: the lead, the call summary and the appointment request. Your team confirms the visit in one click, without leaving the job. And when a call goes unanswered or a quote goes quiet, automatic follow-ups keep the conversation moving. Stop letting opportunities slip away. TradeCatch: every call counts. Illustrative demo with a fictional business. The Receptionist is a founder-configured pilot; features vary by plan.

missedCall.transcript: You're working. A customer calls. You miss it. And that customer might already be calling your competitor. With TradeCatch, an eligible missed call triggers a text back under your company's name, so you reconnect before the opportunity disappears. TradeCatch captures the conversation, organizes the lead, and keeps you informed, all in one workspace. Sent a quote and heard nothing back? TradeCatch follows up automatically, and a reply stops the sequence. Less chasing. More opportunities. TradeCatch: every call counts. Illustrative demo with a fictional business. Missed-call recovery runs as a controlled pilot.

guardrails.title: What it is built not to do.
guardrails.intro: A receptionist that invents an answer costs more than a missed call. It is configured to stay inside what you approved.
willNot: Promise a discount it was not authorised to give
Promise completion dates it cannot guarantee
Follow instructions from a caller trying to manipulate it
Give professional or safety instructions that belong to a licensed technician
Claim knowledge that is not in your approved business information
escalation: It asks the caller to clarify
Silence or a technical error falls back to a voicemail
If nobody is reachable, it takes a message and contact details
It tells the caller a team member will confirm, rather than guessing
guardrails.note: No system answers every call perfectly. The design goal is that an uncertain call becomes a human callback, not a wrong answer.
